documents.unit: Office of the Vice Provost for Academic Excellence
documents.title: Guidance on AI
documents.summary: Manoa's Vice Provost for Academic Excellence page does not set an AI rule. It points to the student code of conduct, which gives instructors authority to define permitted AI assistance, and strongly encourages instructors to be specific, discuss scenarios, and redesign assignments, with a list of strategies. It also encourages experimentation within legal and ethical limits and refers to data and IT policies.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no campus-wide permission or ban. It says the code of conduct 'gives the instructor authority over defining unauthorized assistance, authorized sources, and specifically prohibited behavior' and that instructors are 'strongly encouraged' to be specific, so the decision is handed to instructors, i.e. delegates.

units.why: The opening says AI 'holds promise' and can 'provide new learning modes, personalize learning experiences'; it names benefits without setting a rule, so it is a benefits statement (P87), informs and neutral.
units.anchor: AI-powered tools can provide new learning modes, personalize learning experiences

units.why: The same passage says AI 'can streamline administrative tasks, enhancing efficiency and potentially reducing operational costs', an operational benefit; it is a benefit claim (P87), not a rule on administrative use (P76).
units.anchor: AI can streamline administrative tasks, enhancing efficiency and potentially reducing operational costs

units.why: The document says integration 'raises important questions about data privacy, ethics, algorithmic bias, and the need for faculty and staff preparation'; naming bias and ethics concerns fits P53, chosen because it is the main concern named.
units.anchor: raises important questions about data privacy, ethics, algorithmic bias
units.frag_end: is already reshaping aspects of higher education.
units.fit_note: Also names data privacy and faculty/staff preparation, which P53 does not capture.

units.why: It states the student code of conduct 'gives the instructor authority over defining unauthorized assistance, authorized sources, and specifically prohibited behavior', so the decision on what AI use is allowed sits with each instructor (P04).
units.anchor: gives the instructor authority over defining unauthorized assistance, authorized sources, and specifically prohibited behavior

units.why: The code of conduct 'addresses Cheating, plagiarism, or other forms of academic dishonesty', the basis on which AI misuse is handled under the heading 'AI and Academic Integrity'; closest to P36 though AI is not named in the quote.
units.anchor: addresses “Cheating, plagiarism, or other forms of academic dishonesty.”
units.fit_note: Does not state that AI misuse is misconduct; it only cites the existing code of conduct section under the AI heading.

units.why: 'instructors are strongly encouraged to: Be specific about expectations and limitations on student use of AI in assignments' is a recommendation that instructors state their AI rules; P09 is the nearest type.
units.anchor: Be specific about expectations and limitations on student use of AI in assignments
units.fit_note: Only strongly encouraged, not required; P09 covers a requirement.

units.why: 'Hold students responsible for the accuracy of facts and sources used in assignments' asks instructors to make students accountable for what they submit, matching P29; it is about accuracy of facts and sources, a partial fit.
units.anchor: Hold students responsible for the accuracy of facts and sources used in assignments
units.fit_note: Frames responsibility as accuracy of facts and sources, and as something instructors should enforce.

units.why: 'Talk through scenarios with classes to provide clarity on expectations' recommends discussing AI scenarios in class, which is P66 (explain and discuss the rules) as it goes beyond listing a rule.
units.anchor: Talk through scenarios with classes to provide clarity on expectations

units.why: 'Syllabi and class discussions should make instructor expectations clear with respect to use of AI tools' asks that AI expectations be stated in syllabi; I chose P09 over P66 because the syllabus is named first.
units.anchor: Syllabi and class discussions should make instructor expectations clear with respect to use of AI
units.fit_note: Recommends rather than requires, and names class discussion as well as syllabi.

units.why: 'UHOIC maintains sample statements for adaptation in a syllabus or specific assignments' offers adaptable templates; no type is about providing sample statements, and it is neither tiers nor training.
units.anchor: UHOIC maintains sample statements for adaptation in a syllabus or specific assignments.
units.uncovered_note: The university office maintains sample AI syllabus statements that instructors can adapt for syllabi or assignments.

units.why: The passage says 'assignments and assessments may need redesign to achieve our learning objectives' given AI, comparing it to calculators; it is a statement that assessment should be redesigned around AI (P35).
units.anchor: assignments and assessments may need redesign to achieve our learning objectives
units.fit_note: Frames redesign as a possibility ('may need') tied to learning objectives.

units.why: The first strategy is to 'Chunk assignments with due dates for individual elements that precede final submission: an outline, notes on research articles, and drafts', which restructures assignments around process, so P35.
units.anchor: Chunk assignments with due dates for individual elements

units.why: It suggests instructors 'might consider Google Docs version history and/or draftback' to review students' writing progression; this uses process evidence to spot misuse, so P40.
units.anchor: Google Docs version history and/or

units.why: 'Replace a writing assignment with an audio file, podcast, video, speech, drawing, diagram, or multimedia project' is a format change meant to make 'running to AI more work than it's worth', so assignment redesign (P35).
units.anchor: Replace a writing assignment with an audio file

units.why: 'Incorporate AI. Ask students to generate a ChatGPT response... then write an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses' builds AI into an assignment; I chose P79 over P31 because the instruction is to use AI in the task.
units.anchor: Ask students to generate a ChatGPT response to a question of their own choosing
units.fit_note: Also has students critically evaluate AI output (P31), and is a suggested strategy, not a requirement.

units.why: The list advises to 'Reference class materials or sources that are not available on the internet', an assignment design that AI cannot easily answer, so P35.
units.anchor: Reference class materials or

units.why: 'Include visuals' (images or videos students must respond to) is a redesign tactic against AI-generated answers, so P35.
units.anchor: Include visuals

units.why: 'Connect to current events or conversations in your field' is another suggested redesign tactic in the list, so P35.
units.anchor: current events or conversations in your field

units.why: 'Ask for application of personal knowledge/experience' is a redesign strategy that makes AI answers less usable, so P35.
units.anchor: application of personal knowledge

units.why: 'Employ authentic and contextualized assessments... it is challenging for students to rely solely on AI for complete solutions' recommends assessment redesign and gives the reason, so P35.
units.anchor: authentic and contextualized assessments

units.why: 'Use open-ended questions that prompt students to demonstrate their understanding, creativity...' is a recommended assessment design against direct AI answers, so P35.
units.anchor: open-ended questions

units.why: 'Incorporate elements that evaluate the process students followed... written explanations, justifications, or reflections' asks for process evidence alongside submissions; I chose P35 because these are instructor-designed assessment elements, not student logs of AI use (P26).
units.anchor: evaluate the process students followed
units.fit_note: Also calls for written explanations and reflections, which resemble P26.

units.why: The page points to an 'annotated listing maintained by UHOIC' of AI resources with sections on 'Accessibility, Assessment... Prompting, Tools', which supports instructors learning about AI, so P63.
units.anchor: annotated listing maintained by UHOIC
units.fit_note: Resources cover teaching and learning generally, not only faculty.

units.why: 'Teaching and learning about AI is one piece of a need to assist students in learning appropriate 21st century digital skills' gives a skills reason to teach AI, so P44.
units.anchor: assist students in learning appropriate 21st century digital skills

units.why: 'Experts agree that generative AI tools are here to stay' states AI is not going away, an acknowledgement of limits on control, closest to P82.
units.anchor: generative AI tools are here to stay
units.fit_note: Implies AI is permanent but does not say bans are impractical.

units.why: 'Faculty and students are encouraged to experiment with AI tools while staying within legal and ethical parameters' welcomes AI experimentation with a compliance condition; this is encouragement by default (P02).
units.anchor: encouraged to experiment with AI tools while staying within legal and ethical parameters
units.frag_end: to the best of their ability.
units.fit_note: Also asks to stay within legal and ethical parameters (P77).

units.why: 'university personnel should be aware of policies and procedures that relate to the adoption of new technologies' lists EP 2.219, 2.215 and 2.210 on data protection and IT use, so complying with existing university policy, P77.
units.anchor: university personnel should be aware of policies and procedures that relate to the adoption

units.why: The document points to 'UH Approved 3rd-Party Online Tools' as a list personnel should know, i.e. university-approved tools, P92.
units.anchor: UH Approved 3rd-Party Online Tools
units.fit_note: Only listed as a related resource; not stated as an instruction to use only approved tools.

notes: Single included document. The sample-statements unit is coded UNCOVERED.
